## 3. Calibration summary

| model | calibration_slope | calibration_intercept | brier | brier_skill_vs_prevalence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1.031 | 0.009 | 0.021 | 0.005 |
| B | 0.880 | -0.524 | 0.021 | 0.001 |

A slope near 1 and intercept near 0 mean good calibration; a Brier skill near 0 means the model barely beats always predicting the average rate.

## 4. Precision diagnostic (not a predictor: it uses the outcome year's posterior uncertainty)

Spearman correlation between county population and the posterior uncertainty of the trend: -0.46.

| sdt | pq | rows | events | event_rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| low uncertainty | Q1 smallest | 158 | 1 | 0.006 |
| low uncertainty | Q2 | 274 | 8 | 0.029 |
| low uncertainty | Q3 | 357 | 15 | 0.042 |
| low uncertainty | Q4 largest | 449 | 17 | 0.038 |
| mid | Q1 smallest | 136 | 4 | 0.029 |
| mid | Q2 | 321 | 6 | 0.019 |
| mid | Q3 | 390 | 8 | 0.021 |
| mid | Q4 largest | 390 | 11 | 0.028 |
| high uncertainty | Q1 smallest | 634 | 1 | 0.002 |
| high uncertainty | Q2 | 333 | 5 | 0.015 |
| high uncertainty | Q3 | 181 | 4 | 0.022 |
| high uncertainty | Q4 largest | 89 | 1 | 0.011 |

If event rates fall mainly with uncertainty and stay similar across county-size quartiles inside each uncertainty band, the population effect is largely a detectability effect.
